newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait share index up, trade levels ease in week.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait share index up, trade levels ease in week.

text.p: Kuwait Stock Exchange's index rose 35.4 points in the week to Wednesday while trade levels fell amid cautious dealings, investors said on Thursday.
The market started to recover from a fall caused by the Central Bank's blockage of lending for equity trading, they said.
"People are still cautious," said a dealer.
"The market is restoring confidence after the Central Bank's decision," said a portfolio manager. "There is no liquidity problem."
The Central Bank's curbs on lending for equity trading purposes were announced earlier in June. Trade levels and prices fell after the announcement.
The index finished the week at 2,384.7 points with gainers leading losers 30-16.

But daily average for value of traded shares fell to 45.5 million dinars ($150.6 million) from 61.7 million. Volume eased to a daily average of 155.8 million shares from 223.3 million, Kuwait Stock Exchange (KSE) figures show.

Loans for securities trading in May stood at 425 million dinars ($1.402 million) of which 96 million dinars were margin loans, the Central Bank said. The figure needs to be reduced by 130 million dinars by the end of 1997.
Property firms were the most active sector in terms of traded value with 71.5 million dinars, followed by investment firms with 63 million and industrials with 34 million.
Boubyan Petrochemicals, al-Tamdeen Real Estate, Investment Projects, United Realty and Pearl of Kuwait Real Estate were among the most active shares.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest in mutual funds.
